text:
Hi Colin,

Thanks! I hope you are also doing well.

For the demo, we are hopeful you can perform per-frame-bbox seeded
segmentation of the smoke plume on the provided frames.

For the 2 examples, the bounding boxes we would like to see used as the
prompts, are stored in annotations.json and are frame-matched. (In some
examples, the smoke is far away and disparate so the bounding box seeds the
SAM3 engine for higher precision in EACH frame).

For data security purposes we are limited to sharing 10 frames.

If there are any questions, let me know! I have attached the google drive
link -- here

text:
Hi James,
 
Apologies for the late reply — I was out of office for the past two days.
 
I had already sent the note below to Andrew, but it seems it may not have reached you, so I'm re-sending it here.
 
To be transparent about where we stand: our team is currently building our own data platform in-house, so any external solution would need a strong, well-documented case before we bring more colleagues into the discussion. The current deck is a helpful introduction, but it doesn't yet give us enough technical detail to make a meeting productive. I'd therefore like to suggest we postpone — rather than reschedule to Thursday or Friday — until we can review more concrete material.
 
In particular, it would help us greatly if you could share details on:
 
- Support for autonomous-driving sensor data (multi-camera video, LiDAR point clouds), with a focus on AI-native features beyond annotation and how they differentiate Encord from open-source tools like CVAT.
- The model evaluation workflows referenced in the Woven by Toyota case study.
- Your commercial model, including licensing and pricing.
 
Once we've had a chance to review this information, I'll identify the right teammates to join the discussion and get back to you with some proposed meeting times.
 
Apologies again for the change of plans, and thank you for your understanding.

subject: AW: Encord Commercial Case
text:
Hi Tom,
Thank you for your message and for checking this internally.
As mentioned during yesterday's call, the decision between the different solutions was very close. For a start-up like Telendo, liquidity is the lifeblood of the company, and we therefore pay all of our software subscriptions monthly. The other providers we are considering are also able to offer monthly payment terms.
I have to admit that an annual upfront commitment raises some concern on our side. Is this simply a fixed internal policy, or is there a particular cash-flow shortage behind it? I would appreciate it if you could check once more with your finance team whether monthly or, at minimum, quarterly billing could exceptionally be approved. In our view, the lack of payment flexibility represents a meaningful competitive disadvantage for Encord, particularly when working with early-stage companies.
We will speak again with the alternative providers on Monday to determine whether they can offer a structure that fits our needs.
Encord remains our preferred solution from a technical perspective, but unless some flexibility can be found on the payment terms, it will be difficult for us to proceed with the order form at this stage.
Best regards

Carsten
